transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
I guess… it’s what happens after I eat like that. I sit there looking at the empty containers, and I just feel disgusted with myself. Like I’m not the steady, in-control man I’ve always tried to be.
Can you describe what typically happens when you eat like that? How often do these episodes occur?
Since I’ve been home with my back injury… it’s been several nights most weeks. I don’t think there’s been a single week in the last three months where it didn’t happen at least once.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to compensate for what you’ve eaten?
No… I don’t do that. I just kind of sit with it afterward.
Do these eating episodes cause you significant distress or interfere with your daily life in any way?

Yeah… it does. I’ve, uh… started dodging some of the check-in calls from drivers I was supposed to be mentoring. I just feel embarrassed, like I don’t want them hearing how far off my usual routine I’ve gotten.
When you're eating during these episodes, do you feel like you can't stop or control yourself once you start?
Yeah… once I start, it’s like that discipline I used to have on the road just shuts off. I’ll be telling myself, “Magin, put the fork down,” and my hand still goes back for more.
When you're eating during these episodes, do you find yourself eating much more rapidly than normal?
Yeah… I do. I eat like I’m trying to make a delivery window or something. Too fast. Half the time I’m barely even tasting it.
Do these eating episodes usually happen when you're feeling stressed, anxious, or down about your situation?
I don’t know… I haven’t really pinned it to that. Sometimes I’m not feeling great, sure, but I can’t say it’s always stress or being down that sets it off.
Do you ever find yourself eating even when you’re not physically hungry, especially during these episodes?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I haven’t paid close attention to whether I’m actually hungry or not when it happens. It’s kind of hard to tell in the moment.
Do you usually eat alone during these episodes because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?
I’m not sure. I mean, I do end up by myself a lot, but I haven’t really thought about whether it’s because I’m embarrassed or just because that’s how it happens.
After these eating episodes, do you find yourself feeling guilty, ashamed, or upset with yourself?
Yeah… after, I do. I’ll just sit there and see all the empty containers, and I feel… disgusted with myself. Like I’m not the steady, in-control guy I’ve always tried to be.
During these eating episodes, do you find yourself eating until you feel uncomfortably full?

Yeah… I do. I’ll keep going past the point where I should stop. My stomach gets stretched and hurts, and then with my back, I’m just stuck in the recliner feeling miserable… even getting up feels like too much.
When you're eating during these episodes, do you feel like you can't stop or control yourself once you start?

Yeah… it does feel that way. Once I start, it’s like the discipline I used to have on the road just shuts off. I’ll be telling myself, “Magin, put the fork down,” but my hand just keeps going back for more.
During these eating episodes, do you feel like you’re not in control of what or how much you’re eating?
Yeah… I’m not really in control then. Once I start, it’s like whatever discipline I used to have just shuts off. I’ll be telling myself, “Magin, put the fork down,” but… my hand keeps going back.
